why: FAO 2019 (ca5644en.pdf) p.9 names 'varieties of sugars' (class) among ultra-processed ingredients and PMC10127522 (Martinez Steele et al., J Nutr 2022;153(1):225-241) (table footnote 12, 'Other ultraprocessed foods') codes 'all syrups (excluding 100% maple syrup)' as ultra-processed: class-instance (glucose syrup in liquid form); FAO Group 2 names only maple syrup among syrups, so no conflict. STRONG marker proposal for the owner.

NUPENS 'Food classification Nova' page (nupens.fsp.usp.br/en/food-classification-nova/) (group 4) lists 'protein isolates or concentrates' among the substances of ultra-processed formulations and Monteiro et al., Lancet 2025 'Ultra-processed foods and human health: the main thesis and the evidence' (fsp.usp.br PDF) names 'plant protein isolates'; FAO p.9 names 'soya protein isolate' (existing marker 'protein isolate'). Texturized soy protein as an instance of that class is an INFERENCE (extruded product of soy protein concentrate or flour). STRONG marker proposal for the owner.
